note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect and until is derived by hand from the 55-wire ER-32 list and the p.12 purpose, not printed. Topology: relay 3 is the paid latch (3G(+)-3H-3F), fed by pb4 through 4J-4H-3J-3H; 3L-3K lights output 1, 3L-3N lights output 2. Relay 4 pulls in from the relay 3 latch when pb4 is released and arms Drive Away: pb3 via 4L-4K-4H-4G drops relay 3 (re-set), while with relay 4 out pb3 via 4L-4N-2F latches relay 2 (2H-2G), whose 2L-2K feeds indicator 1 and the self-interrupting relay 1 (alarm). Relays 5/6 form a nickel toggle on the pb5 / D5 / D10 node; with ER-32 as printed their only exit, 6L-6K-5N, ends at relay 5 set 2 whose arm 5L is unwired, so two nickels and ten pennies do not pay and Drive Away then sounds the alarm. That contradicts p.13 and is the O-C8 manual defect; the 5L/6G-kept variant (step7-notes) is a different wiring and is not this fixture. Assumptions: a lamp-limited coil (nF fed, nE to its indicator and output lamps) pulls in, as relay 3 must for the printed payment; relay 4 holds through relay 3 transfer gap on Drive Away and relay 6 through relay 5 transfer gap on the second nickel. Not asserted: lamps lit only through a coil in series, relay 1 between buzz strokes, relays 5/6 after the penny run (depends on the D5 dwell against relay 5 drop-out, O-R1/O-R3/O-R5), the dial rest after the D0 stop (coast O-R5), and one nickel plus five pennies (with relays 5/6 set, the wiper on D5 feeds the motor through coil 5, 5E-6G-6H-D5-D16-D18, a creep path the topology does not settle). Script choices: dial set to 0 before power-on; a power cycle before the penny case; 300 ms dwells; pb6 released as the dial reaches c0. Digest is a placeholder for the runner.
